data.title: A $14.5M Lemon deal and a new D3 vault — What is Tether doing?
data.description:
Stablecoin giant Tether [USDT] has been making some moves lately. Here’s the rundown.

A $14.5M investment into Lemon, but…

… only $5M buys equity.

Tether has backed Argentine fintech app Lemon, with the former not putting a number on it when it announced the deal. Lemon did, however, saying that the package is worth $14.5 million.

Is there a catch? Yes.

According to Lemon CEO Marcelo Cavazzoli, only $5 million of that is an actual investment in the company’s shares. The other $9.5 million is an incentive plan linked to products the two will build together.

There’s a lot that’s unclear right now though. Neither side has shared Lemon’s valuation or how big a stake Tether is getting. There’s also no word on how or when the $9.5 million gets paid out. Tether is after more users for USDT and Tether Gold [XAUT] across Latin America. Lemon gives it a decent shot at that. The app is said to have 4.5 million verified users, and its main balance runs on USDT.

Worth noting, however, that Lemon’s not the only home for Tether this month.

USDT on D3’s domain platform through a Sentora-run vault

On the 9th, D3 launched a USD vault for Tether’s stablecoin. Users can deposit USDT, keep an eye on their position, and withdraw without leaving the platform.

Sentora built the system using its Earn OS and Upshift tools, which decide where deposited funds go. Money moves with the market, within a set of risk rules. It is said that the setup has already handled more than $2 billion.

But why a vault?

Domain buyers usually come in, make a deal, and leave. Earning on stablecoins gives them a reason to keep their money on the platform.

Just don’t mistake automated for guaranteed. Returns depend on the lending markets the vault uses. So, users are still trusting a whole stack of infrastructure with their dollars.

Final Summary

  • Tether has backed Lemon with $14.5M, but only $5M is equity.
  • USDT is now on D3 through a Sentora-run yield vault.

data.title: Fidelity files for Spot Chainlink ETF as LINK climbs 5.5% – Details
data.description:
In a recent turn of events, Fidelity Investments filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to launch a spot Chainlink [LINK] exchange-traded product (ETP). 

All about Fidelity’s S-1 registration

According to the 25th November filing, the proposed fund is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the provisional ticker FLNK. That said, the fund would also hold LINK tokens directly. This allows investors to gain exposure to LINK through traditional stock market accounts without having to purchase or manage the tokens themselves.

At the same time, the fund aims to track the Fidelity Chainlink Reference Rate, which calculates LINK’s price using a volume-weighted median methodology based on data from eligible spot markets.

 Notably, its holdings would be managed by three proposed custodians, including Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust, and Coinbase Custody Trust Company.

LINK’s price action and ETF analysis

As expected, this news did have a positive impact on LINK’s price, which was trading at $9.16 at press time after a hike of 5.5% in the past 24 hours. With this, Fidelity becomes the third asset manager to launch a LINK ETF besides Grayscale’s GLNK and Bitwise’s CLNK.

In fact, according to SoSo Value data, GLNK and CLNK have already recorded cumulative net inflows of $128.12 million and $47.88 million, respectively. This in turn has brought their combined cumulative inflows to approximately $176 million. However, neither fund recorded any new flows on the 25th of November, with both showing $0 in daily net inflows. 

How did other ETFs perform? 

This news comes as the broader cryptocurrency investment products recorded widespread outflows across major digital assets in the month of November. Starting with Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs, which witnessed the largest withdrawals, worth approximately $5.39 billion in net outflows, facing their worst month since launch.

Ethereum [ETH] ETFs too saw $1.30 billion worth of outflows. This was followed by XRP ETFs, which saw $29.18 million in outflows, while Solana [SOL] ETFs registered withdrawals of $57 million. Meanwhile, Dogecoin [DOGE] ETFs recorded relatively smaller outflows of $409,130.

Interestingly, not all products experienced negative flows, as HBAR ETFs attracted approximately $1.71 million in net inflows. This made it the only asset in the sea of ETFs to record positive flows on the day.

Final Summary

  • The proposed fund is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the provisional ticker FLNK.
  • Grayscale’s GLNK and Bitwise’s CLNK recorded cumulative net inflows of $128.12 million and $47.88 million, respectively.

data.title: XRP price eyes $1 – But THESE signals warn traders to stay cautious
data.description:
Ripple [XRP] was up 3.46% in the past 24 hours, with a daily trading volume uptick of 34%. The price bounce followed a Bitcoin [BTC] move back above $61k, which was likely a result of a short squeeze.

This price bounce was reflected across the altcoin market, which has gained 1.72% in its cumulative market cap in a day, reaching $2.07 trillion at the time of writing.

XRP was about to test the $1 resistance zone, a place it had faced rejection from earlier this week. Can the bulls succeed in reclaiming it as support this time?

Is the consolidation phase underway for XRP?

In September and October, XRP was oscillating between the $1.30 support zone and the $1.50-$1.55 supply zone. This consolidation gave way to a downtrend that reached a low below $0.90.

Over the past two weeks, the $0.893 and $1.00 levels have emerged as key levels on the daily timeframe for swing traders. A daily session close outside these boundaries will likely decide the direction of the next swing price move.

At press time, the CMF was at -0.12, signaling heavy selling pressure and capital outflows. The MACD was also moving below the zero line, a sign that downward momentum was prevalent. The MACD line made a bullish crossover above the signal line, an indication of short-term bounce potential.

Despite encouraging ETF flows over the past year, the altcoin’s performance had been lacklustre.

The trend was now firmly bearish, the Directional Movement Index asserted. This indicator’s -DI and ADX readings above 20 confirmed the downtrend, alongside the price structure.

Should XRP traders stay in the range?

Like the 1-day chart showed a sweep above $1 on Monday, XRP recently made a sweep of the $0.961 local peak in recent hours. Despite the short-term upward momentum, there is a chance of a pullback.

Potential buyers can wait to see the price reaction from the $0.92 and $0.86-$0.88 demand zones.

A bullish reaction on the hourly chart, in the form of something like an engulfing candle, would be a sign that bulls were ready to drive a move toward $1.00.

Traders should be wary of short-term volatility and wait for a positive reaction before buying. Risk-averse traders can remain sidelined until the higher timeframe trend gives a new direction with a move beyond $1.00 or $0.893.

Final Summary

  • XRP was one of the top altcoins with a sizeable price bounce in the past 24 hours.
  • Bulls were readying to make a move toward $1.00, but might face a correction toward $0.88 or $0.92 in the short term.

data.title: Inside Bitcoin’s $16B short liquidation zone: Could BTC bears get squeezed again?
data.description:
Bitcoin [BTC] witnessed yet another bout of volatility this week that caught the bulls off guard. On Wednesday, the 25th of November, Bitcoin bounced from a low of $57,300 to a local high of $61,622.

This bounce spurred the rest of the crypto market higher too, resulting in $406.85 million in long liquidations and $238.06 million in short liquidations.

Why is Bitcoin up today?

The U.S. personal consumption expenditures (PCE) data was released on Wednesday. It rose 3.8% year-over-year, while core PCE rose 3.3% year-over-year.

Headline PCE in line with consensus estimates reinforced the market expectations of a 25-bps Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

A week ago, there was a 6.5% probability of a 50-point rate hike. At the time of writing, this probability was 0%.

It wasn’t bullish news, but it was a catalyst that allowed the price to jump higher and wipe out the dense cluster of short positions that had built up in recent days. Monday’s rally just past $64k was another short squeeze.

As things stand, demand is too weak and pessimism too intense for Bitcoin to mount an immediate comeback.

Founder and CEO of intelligence platform CryptoQuant, Ki Young Ju, noted that there was $16 billion in potential short liquidations from $60k to $100k, compared to just $5 billion in potential long liquidations.

In other words, a short squeeze was much more attractive in these conditions. Notably, a mini short squeeze occurred on Monday, as well as the recent price bounce back above $61k.

Bitcoin selling might not have finished

The Bitcoin active value to investor value ratio was back near 0.8 after climbing above 1.0 earlier this year, reported a crypto analyst. Moreno. It measures how far the spot price deviates from the True Market Mean, which is the aggregate on-chain cost basis for active investors.

Readings below 1 indicate active investors are carrying losses. Aggregate profitability has deteriorated since the BTC price rebound earlier this year.

The Bitcoin risk index was above 2 and neared its peak value from earlier this year. The metric shows higher readings during sell-offs, when capital turnover intensifies relative to market value.

The two metrics showed increasing stress on the market and offered a more attractive valuation to long-term buyers.

To make a compelling case for a bullish recovery, the selling pressure needs to be absorbed. The evidence at hand does not support sizeable demand- for example, Bitcoin spot ETF flows have been overwhelmingly bearish in November.

Final Summary

  • The Bitcoin price bounce in the past 12 hours was likely a result of a short squeeze.
  • Metrics show sustained pressure on BTC and no sign of sustained demand yet to support the idea of a trend reversal.

data.title: HYPE’s price hits August low after 7% price drop — What next?
data.description:
Hyperliquid [HYPE] fell by 7.39% over the last 24 hours, a significant drop compared to the rest of the crypto market. The timing here is interesting since the slump followed Abraxas Capital reportedly exiting its Hyperliquid positions, selling 219,081 HYPE tokens estimated to be worth $13.25 million.

The wider market’s weakness has added to the uncertainty and pressure, with Bitcoin ETF outflows and extreme fear weighing on sentiment and keeping HYPE’s near-term outlook bearish.

Bearish pressure mounts on the daily timeframe

HYPE was trading at $57.85 on the daily chart, within the 0%-23.6% Fibonacci zone. The decline resulted in the token being pushed below a price level it had managed to defend since mid-August, marking a potential shift in its overall price trend.

Furthermore, the RSI fell to 28.43, putting HYPE firmly in oversold territory as momentum remained bearish and sellers retained their control of the market. Also, the falling OBV seemed to suggest that buying volume has been unable to overcome the sustained selling pressure.

HYPE sellers regain control on the 4-hour chart

The 4-hour chart hinted at a similar story, with HYPE also trading within the 0%-23.6% Fibonacci zone and below the $59.25-level. Failure to reclaim this threshold has been keeping the immediate price structure bearish, leaving the $55.85 swing low completely exposed.

The MACD continued its bearish trajectory too, suggesting that the bear run was still in full swing. The OBV also slumped significantly, indicating that selling volume has been outweighing buying activity lately.

The 4-hour chart’s weakness seemed to be reinforcing the bearish signals on the daily chart. This leaves HYPE vulnerable to another leg lower.

Final Summary

  • HYPE has officially broken below a price level for the first time since mid-August, paving the way for a potential shift in its broader price structure.
  • 4-hour chart remains under pressure, with HYPE trading below $59.25.

data.title: Is Venice AI really private? VVV crypto falls after researcher’s latest claims
data.description:
Venice AI’s [VVV] promise? What you type stays between you and the screen.

However, now it looks like that’s not happening. And, the native token is taking a hit.

Researcher alleges Venice AI sends prompts to 5 outside providers

Earlier today, a researcher who goes by adacyborg11 posted a list of unflattering claims on X. 

According to these accusations, Venice AI reportedly passes a lot of user requests to outside providers. The names mentioned included DeepInfra, Fireworks, Baseten, Parasail and fal.ai.

The researcher also claimed that public keys are being sent without encryption, something that could leave chats open to people who shouldn’t see them. Seven of Venice’s 21 database tables were said to be unencrypted, with adacyborg11 also stating that the keys meant to lock up chat data could be stored in plain text.

Users may not always get the model they pick either. Some reportedly received answers from a different model than the one they chose.

In addition, claims were also made that Venice is in violation of EU and UK privacy rules, with no cookie consent banners and or age checks.

VVV crypto falls 15% from its high after allegations

The altcoin climbed from $24.5 yesterday to just above $30.5 in the early hours of today. Soon after, things took a turn for the worse.

One hourly candle wiped out a big chunk of the gains, with the price falling by 15% to about $25.8. It came with the heaviest selling volume on the chart as well. At press time, VVV was valued at $26.69 on the charts.

To be fair, the rally was already running hot. The RSI was pushing 80 before the drop, which is why some of this could be traders cashing out. At the time of writing, it had calmed down to hit 45.5, under its average.

The CMF was at 0.15, implying that more money was still coming in than going out. However, it was still down from 0.40 at its peak, with the same sliding down all day.

Have the buyers given up? Well, not really. However, they’re certainly not showing the same interest they were before.

Final Summary

  • A researcher claimed that Venice AI sends user prompts to five outside providers.
  • VVV fell by about 15% from its high.

data.title: 1Password confirms data breach – Could users face phishing attacks?
data.description:
1Password confirmed a breach on the 25th of November after an attacker copied customer records through compromised backend systems.

The company said password vaults remained protected, while the stolen information raised the risk of convincing impersonation attempts. For those unaware, 1Password is a password manager that stores passwords, passkeys, and other sensitive information in encrypted digital vaults.

What did attackers take?

1Password began investigating on the 19th of November after an attacker compromised an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker used that access to push malicious code into backend services and download records for some customers.

Those included names, email addresses, account identifiers, creation and sign-in times, and non-secret technical metadata. The attacker also copied public keys, authentication parameters, and tokens from certain invitation, provisioning, and account recovery links.

1Password said those tokens alone could not grant access; users also needed to complete sign-in or email verification. The attacker also copied private source code and accessed the company’s software deployment systems.

However, it stated that it never stored account passwords or Secret Keys required to decrypt vaults.

The company disabled the compromised account and rotated potentially exposed credentials. It reported no internal evidence of account takeovers through exposed provisioning tokens.

How did they get in?

The reassurance about vaults left a separate question hanging: how had one employee account enabled such extensive access?

Akash Network founder Greg Osuri said his trust was “heavily diminished” and called for an option to keep vaults entirely local. Crypto and blockchain CTO Nicki Sanders focused on the intrusion, stating,

The part that worries me is how they got in.

Trading Strategy co-founder Mikko Ohtamaa favored open-source alternatives, arguing that transparency could make persistent attacks easier to detect.

Others were less categorical. X user Tom Lombardi called the incident,

Bad, but not a deal killer.

The disagreement extended to passwords themselves. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) urged users to change all passwords.

After 1Password said passwords remained unexposed, CZ acknowledged the clarification and suggested weak-password checks and changing login emails to protect against phishing.

Could stolen records fuel crypto phishing?

Stolen account details could help scammers impersonate 1Password through convincing recovery messages. That risk already reaches beyond email.

Unit 42 research tracked fake IT-support voice calls targeting over 150 employees across at least ten companies. The activity ran between January and April 2026.

Binance’s official risk account previously documented WhatsApp impersonators using supposed P2P account problems to solicit login QR-code scans. Ledger’s campaign tracker documented fake support calls and physical letters directing recipients toward recovery-phrase theft.

Final Summary

  • The attacker copied customer records, recovery-related tokens, and private source code after compromising an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
  • 1Password said vaults remained protected and passwords stayed unexposed. Still, stolen account details could help scammers craft convincing phishing messages.

data.title: Ethereum maps post-AI, post-quantum cryptographic overhaul with Keccak-256 — Details
data.description:
Ethereum Foundation is in the news today after it announced that it has recommended Keccak-256 as the hash function for Ethereum’s hash-based cryptography.

The ongoing bear market price action is only a bump in the road. In the long term, however, the network has to be prepared to contend with threats posed by both quantum computing and progressing artificial intelligence capabilities.

Keccak-256 preferred for its large security margin, native integration

On Tuesday, 24th November, the Foundation revealed its recommendation and the reasons behind it.

It considered five candidates: the ZK-friendly hashes, Poseidon and Poseidon2, the fast hashes BLAKE3 and BLAKE2, and the two hashes Ethereum already uses- SHA-256 and Keccak-256.

Keccak-256 has “arguably the most extensive cryptanalysis out of all unbroken traditional hashes,” the blog post read. An additional benefit is that this hash function has so far remained unaffected by AI-assisted cryptanalysis

Zero-knowledge proof technology improvements have removed the performance advantages offered by Poseidon. Security was the primary concern.

Though natively fast, the best collision attack reached 38 out of 64 rounds for SHA-256. Only 5 out of 24 rounds were reached for Keccak-256.

The Foundation also recommended against using SHA3-256 alongside Keccak-256 since both use the same underlying permutation and have similar security characteristics.

AI is a “more urgent risk” than quantum computers

According to Ethereum Foundation Researcher Kev Wedderburn, they have been planning ways to counter quantum computing’s threat. In fact, AI has emerged as a more urgent risk recently.

Models are already finding bugs in production software faster than people can review them, the researcher wrote.

The planned upgrade will overhaul how validators sign messages, users authorize transactions, and how Ethereum verifies data posted by rollups.

It is harder than the 2022 Merge, and there is less time, Wedderburn acknowledged. Working faster can ship more bugs, so the Foundation has doubled the protocol security team to ensure formal verification. This will also allow the security work to progress at the pace of protocol development.

Final Summary

  • The Ethereum Foundation has recommended Keccak-256 over four other hash functions, citing its security track record.
  • Artificial intelligence models are finding bugs in production software faster than people can review them.

data.title: Could Bitwise’s $667M XRP ETF inflows come to the rescue as bear trap takes shape?
data.description:
Bitwise has released its annual XRP ETF report.

According to the report, the ETF has seen net cash flows of $667 million since it began trading on the NYSE in November 2025. Meanwhile, assets under management were in excess of $376 million while total trading crossed $3.5 billion, averaging around $14 million a day.  

In essence, despite XRP’s lackluster performance, interest in the ETF continues to receive institutional investment, implying a high level of investor demand.

In a post on X, Bitwise highlighted XRP’s decade-long presence in the crypto market. It also noted how the asset has remained relevant through multiple market cycles and continues to shape the industry’s future. 

XRP has been part of crypto’s story for more than a decade, through every cycle, and it’s still helping shape what comes next. We’re grateful to everyone who’s been part of the journey so far. Here’s to year two! 

The timing is particularly interesting here.

Bitwise’s report comes as XRP’s technical and on-chain metrics continue to deteriorate. Meanwhile, prediction markets are also increasingly pricing in a year-end target below $0.80. Against this backdrop, the key question is whether Bitwise’s report can strengthen institutional interest and turn the current bearish setup into a bear trap.

Institutional FOMO could catch XRP bears off gaurd

The impact of Bitwise’s one-year XRP ETF performance could already be triggering FOMO.

Notably, another Wall Street firm has disclosed exposure to an XRP ETF. Atlanta-based Arkadios Wealth Advisors, which looks after $8.79 billion in client assets, stated this in its most recent SEC document.

Furthermore, there is some institutional interest in Turkiye too. One of the nation’s biggest private banks, Yapi Kredi, is leveraging Ripple Custody to provide digital asset security solutions. 

The key takeaway? XRP’s derivatives continue to be significantly net short, with the long/short ratio showing a pronounced sell-side sentiment. At the time of writing, XRP seemed set to close its 10th consecutive weekly down candle, with broader market FUD and prediction markets pricing in a year-end target below $0.80 to reinforce the cautious outlook.

Interestingly, however, the XRP/BTC ratio has risen by almost 5% following three successive weeks of upside.

In essence, broader market weakness could create room for more capital to flow into XRP.

This makes it an important setup to watch over the coming months. The logic is simple —  Entering Q4, market participants are already factoring in further downside potential. In this context, Bitwise’s recent report, growing ETF exposure, and Ripple’s expansion in Turkiye could encourage further capital rotation into XRP.

If this trend continues, XRP’s ongoing consolidation around $0.90 could turn out to be an accumulation phase before a potential bear trap.

Final Summary
